work.name: Gapstars, placed at Envision AI Labs (Leiden, Netherlands)
highlights: Chose the retrieval embedding model on evidence: built a synthetic question–answer benchmark linked to source records and compared four leading models on recall, nDCG and MRR, with significance tests
Building a ground-truth benchmark from client-provided documents to measure retrieval and answer quality on real data
Designed the evaluation framework for RAG and agentic systems using LLM-as-a-judge metrics, claim-level faithfulness checks and expert-validated gold-standard datasets
Built and benchmarked LLM-based insight-generation features on client-approved pharmaceutical and clinical data
Contributed to the multi-agent architecture behind narrative trend generation: hybrid retrieval, guardrails, citation grounding and context management

work.name: Arcadea Group
highlights: Automated structured data extraction from a US state police agency's records with an offline multi-agent system of 10+ planning, generation, execution and evaluation agents that write named-group regex patterns
Made accuracy verifiable with a generate–test–revise loop scored against ground truth, delivering a validated, reusable regex instead of an ongoing model dependency
Built a customer-care assistant grounded in company knowledge and historical phone calls, comparing traditional RAG with graph-based RAG and adding topic modelling and source traceability

work.name: Surge Global
highlights: Led AI delivery of an orchestrated multi-agent system for an insurance warranty-claims intermediary, giving service technicians a ready recommendation for each claim
Researched connecting a real-time GPT-4o voice agent to multi-agent workflows for a founder relationship assistant

work.name: Surge Global
highlights: First author of iSelf-Discover, showing unstructured reasoning plans beat structured JSON plans across BBH, T4D and MATH (up to 18.9% relative on MATH)
Co-developed OpenBezoar, a low-cost recipe for small open instruction-following models (synthetic data, QLoRA SFT, DPO)
Wrote nanoJAXGPT, a JAX/Equinox rewrite of nanoGPT, as a teaching resource

work.name: StemLink
highlights: Teach an applied LLM curriculum: transformers, prompting, agents (LangChain, LangGraph, AutoGen), RAG (LlamaIndex, Pinecone) and LoRA/QLoRA fine-tuning
Supervise capstone builds through to working demos
